children.title: PART I
children.summary: PART I provides an overview of Verizon Communications Inc.'s business operations, including its service offerings, competitive landscape, and technological advancements. It discusses risk factors affecting the company, such as operational, economic, regulatory, and financial risks. The section confirms there are no unresolved staff comments on financial reporting, details Verizon's significant properties and investments, and outlines the absence of major legal proceedings related to environmental regulations. Additionally, it states there are no mine safety disclosures required, indicating compliance with relevant regulations.

children.title: Item 1. Business
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive overview of Verizon Communications Inc.'s business operations, including its consumer and business services, distribution strategies, competitive landscape, and technological advancements. It details the company's service offerings, including wireless, networking, and IoT solutions, while emphasizing its extensive network and customer demographics. Additionally, it discusses human capital resources, intellectual property rights, regulatory compliance, and the importance of executive leadership. The section also includes cautionary statements regarding forward-looking statements and the availability of financial reports on Verizon's website.

children.title: General
children.summary: The General section provides an overview of Verizon Communications Inc.'s consumer and business services. It details the Verizon Consumer Group, which includes wireless and wireline communications, highlighting significant revenue figures and customer connections as of December 31, 2021. The section also covers the Verizon Business Group, focusing on services for businesses and government entities, including various communication solutions and IoT services, along with its revenue contributions and customer demographics. Overall, it emphasizes Verizon's extensive network and service offerings across different market segments.

children.title: Verizon Consumer Group
children.summary: The Verizon Consumer Group section outlines Verizon Communications Inc.'s consumer-focused services, including wireless and wireline communications. It highlights the extensive wireless network in the U.S. and the provision of fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband. The section details the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc. and reports that the Consumer segment generated $95.3 billion in revenue in 2021, accounting for approximately 71% of Verizon's total revenues. Additionally, it provides statistics on customer connections, including 115 million wireless retail connections and 7 million wireline broadband connections as of December 31, 2021.

children.title: Verizon Business Group
children.summary: The Verizon Business Group section outlines the company's offerings in wireless and wireline communications services targeted at businesses, government entities, and carriers. It details the range of products including data, video, conferencing, corporate networking solutions, and Internet of Things (IoT) services. In 2021, the Business segment generated $31.0 billion in revenue, accounting for approximately 23% of Verizon's total revenues, with around 27 million wireless retail postpaid connections and 477 thousand wireline broadband connections. The section also categorizes services by customer groups such as Small and Medium Business, Global Enterprise, and Public Sector.

children.title: Service and Product Offerings
children.summary: The Service and Product Offerings section details Verizon's comprehensive wireless services and equipment for both Consumer and Business segments. It includes information on network coverage, retail connections, and the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc., as well as various service plans and device options. The Verizon Consumer Group subsection highlights distinctions between postpaid and prepaid services, internet access options, and features available to consumers. The Verizon Business Group subsection outlines tailored offerings for different market segments, detailing revenue contributions and diverse services such as wireless, networking, security, and IoT solutions. Overall, the section emphasizes Verizon's commitment to providing extensive connectivity solutions across various customer bases.

children.title: Wireless
children.summary: The Wireless section covers Verizon's extensive wireless services and equipment offerings for both Consumer and Business segments. It details the network coverage in the U.S., the number of retail connections, and the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc. The section also describes various wireless devices available, payment options, and service plans, including postpaid and prepaid choices. Additionally, it highlights features such as data sharing, high-definition services, and fixed connectivity solutions for mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs).

children.title: Wireless Services
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's wireless services, detailing offerings for both Consumer and Business segments. It highlights the extensive wireless network coverage in the U.S. and the availability of fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband. The Consumer segment serves approximately 115 million wireless retail connections, while the Business segment has around 27 million wireless retail postpaid connections. Additionally, it mentions the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc. and the provision of services on both postpaid and prepaid bases, catering to various customer needs.

children.title: Wireless Equipment
children.summary: This section details Verizon's wireless equipment offerings for both Consumer and Business customers, including smartphones, tablets, and connected devices like smartwatches. It explains the payment options available for acquiring devices, such as installment plans. The section also highlights the variety of service plans offered, including postpaid and prepaid options, and the features included in these plans, such as data sharing and high-definition services. Additionally, it mentions the availability of fixed connectivity solutions and network access services for mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs).

children.title: Verizon Consumer Group
children.summary: The Verizon Consumer Group section outlines the company's offerings in wireless and residential fixed connectivity services. It details the distinction between postpaid and prepaid wireless services, highlighting that as of December 31, 2021, there were 24 million prepaid connections, largely due to the Tracfone acquisition. The section also describes the variety of service plans available, including features like unlimited voice and data, and the availability of internet access through both fiber-optic and traditional copper networks. Additionally, it mentions the provision of network access services to mobile virtual network operators and the range of wireless equipment offered to consumers.

children.title: Verizon Business Group
children.summary: The Verizon Business Group section outlines the company's tailored offerings for various market segments, including Small and Medium Business, Global Enterprise, Public Sector and Other, and Wholesale. It details revenue contributions from each segment, with Small and Medium Business generating $11.8 billion, Global Enterprise $10.2 billion, Public Sector and Other $6.3 billion, and Wholesale $2.7 billion in 2021. The section emphasizes Verizon's diverse services such as wireless, networking, security, and IoT solutions, designed to meet the specific needs of small businesses, large enterprises, government entities, and other carriers. Additionally, it highlights Verizon's distribution strategies and commitment to enhancing service accessibility across these segments.

children.title: Small and Medium Business
children.summary: The Small and Medium Business section outlines Verizon's offerings specifically tailored for U.S.-based small and medium enterprises, which include wireless services, conferencing, voice and networking products, and Fios services. In 2021, this segment generated $11.8 billion in revenue, accounting for approximately 38% of the Business Group's total revenue. The services provided are designed to meet the unique needs of smaller businesses, offering fixed connectivity solutions similar to those available to residential customers, as well as advanced IT services and security solutions. Additionally, the section highlights the integration of features and pricing strategies aimed at enhancing service accessibility for small and medium businesses.

children.title: Global Enterprise
children.summary: The Global Enterprise section details Verizon's services tailored for large businesses and non-U.S. public sector customers, generating $10.2 billion in revenue in 2021, which is about 33% of the Business's total revenues. It outlines a diverse range of offerings including network services, advanced communications, security services, core telecommunications, and IoT services aimed at optimizing operations and mitigating risks. Additionally, it briefly mentions the Public Sector and Other segment, which provides similar services to government and educational institutions, and the Wholesale segment that caters to other carriers, contributing $6.3 billion and $2.7 billion in revenues respectively. The section emphasizes Verizon's comprehensive distribution strategy through various channels to reach its consumer and business customers effectively.

children.title: Public Sector and Other
children.summary: The Public Sector and Other section details Verizon's offerings to U.S. federal, state, and local governments, as well as educational institutions, generating $6.3 billion in revenue in 2021, which is about 20% of the Business's total revenues. It highlights services similar to those provided by Global Enterprise, tailored for governmental and educational needs, including wireless products, wireline connectivity, and managed solutions. Additionally, it covers solutions for fleet tracking, compliance management, field service management, and asset tracking, emphasizing Verizon's commitment to supporting public sector operations.

children.title: Wholesale
children.summary: The Wholesale section details Verizon's wireline communications services, which include data, voice, local dial tone, and broadband services primarily aimed at local, long distance, and wireless carriers. In 2021, Wholesale generated $2.7 billion in revenue, accounting for about 9% of the Business's total revenues. Key offerings include data services to enhance networks, switched access voice services for call completion, and local services for competitive local exchange carriers, including compliance-related offerings. The section highlights the competitive landscape, noting that a significant portion of revenue comes from large telecommunications companies that are also competitors.

children.title: Distribution
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's distribution strategy, which employs a mix of direct, indirect, and alternative channels to reach both Consumer and Business customers. Key components include company-operated stores, sales and service centers, and business direct sales teams, all of which are integral to the direct channel. Additionally, Verizon emphasizes a strong digital and omni-channel experience to enhance customer choice and convenience in accessing their products and services.

children.title: Competition and Related Trends
children.summary: This section discusses the competitive landscape of the telecommunications industry, highlighting the intense competition faced by the company from both traditional and non-traditional service providers. Key competitors include major wireless carriers like AT&T and T-Mobile, as well as resellers and emerging players like DISH Network, which is launching a 5G network. The section outlines critical competitive factors such as network reliability, pricing strategies, and the shift towards over-the-top (OTT) services. It also notes the impact of technological advancements, regulatory changes, and customer preferences on market dynamics.

children.title: Global Network and Technology
children.summary: The Global Network and Technology section covers Verizon's advancements in network architecture, focusing on the transition to an Intelligent Edge Network and the deployment of 5G technology, which offers higher throughput and lower latency compared to 4G LTE. It details the operational status of 5G services in numerous U.S. cities and emphasizes the importance of 4G LTE as the primary platform for wireless traffic. The section also discusses strategies for enhancing wireless network reliability, including small cell technology and redundancy measures. Additionally, it highlights the growth of Fios broadband services, the extensive global IP network supporting business connectivity, and the management of spectrum licenses for mobile and fixed services.

children.title: Network Evolution
children.summary: This section discusses the transformation of network architecture into an Intelligent Edge Network, which aims to enhance efficiency, virtualization, and automation while supporting edge computing services. It highlights the expected benefits of this new architecture, including the simplification of operations, elimination of legacy elements, and accelerated deployment of 5G technology. Additionally, it outlines the advancements in 5G deployment, emphasizing its potential for higher throughput and lower latency compared to 4G LTE, and notes the current availability of 5G services in various U.S. cities.

children.title: 5G Deployment
children.summary: This section discusses the deployment of 5G wireless technology, highlighting its expected advantages over 4G LTE, such as higher throughput and lower latency. It notes the increasing demand for network capacity due to the growth of internet-connected devices. As of December 31, 2021, 5G Ultra Wideband is operational in parts of 87 U.S. cities, while 5G Home is available in parts of 65 U.S. cities. The section emphasizes the company's leadership in developing 5G industry standards and ecosystems for both fixed and mobile services.

children.title: 4G LTE
children.summary: This section discusses the 4G LTE network, which is the primary platform for Verizon's wireless traffic, covering approximately 328 million people as of December 31, 2021. It highlights the advantages of 4G LTE over 3G, including higher data throughput at lower costs, and mentions the collaboration with rural carriers to enhance coverage. The section also outlines strategies for network reliability, including densification through small cell technology and the deployment of advanced technologies to increase capacity. Additionally, it addresses the importance of securing site rights and governmental approvals for network expansion and the use of backup systems to ensure service reliability.

children.title: Wireless Network Reliability and Build-Out
children.summary: This section discusses the importance of wireless network reliability, coverage, and speed for Verizon's success. It outlines strategies for maintaining network quality, including increasing network density through small cell technology and deploying new technologies. The section also highlights the need for securing site rights and obtaining governmental approvals for network build-out. Additionally, it details redundancy measures, such as battery backups and generators, to enhance service reliability, and mentions roaming agreements that extend service coverage for customers.

children.title: Fios
children.summary: The Fios section discusses the growth of residential broadband service, highlighting a significant increase in bandwidth demand driven by new video services, data applications, and IP devices. It emphasizes the advantages of Passive Optical Network (PON) technology, which supports both consumer and business broadband needs. The section also notes the expansion of PON infrastructure in the Business segment as companies shift towards Ethernet-based access services. Overall, it outlines Verizon's strategy to meet increasing data speed and throughput requirements efficiently.

children.title: Global IP
children.summary: Verizon operates one of the largest global fiber-optic networks, providing connectivity to business customers in over 180 countries. The global IP network comprises long-haul, metro, and submarine assets that support international operations. As businesses shift towards an 'everything-as-a-service' model, there is an increasing demand for cloud-based, converged enterprise solutions. Verizon is deploying packet optical transport technology to enhance its global network platform and meet these evolving customer needs.

children.title: Spectrum
children.summary: This section details the spectrum licenses held by Verizon, which are utilized for mobile and fixed wireless voice, video, and data services. It specifies the frequency bands licensed by the FCC, including 800 MHz, 1800-1900 MHz, 700 MHz, and various AWS bands, covering nearly the entire U.S. population. The section discusses the deployment of 4G and 5G technologies using low, mid, and millimeter wave spectrum, including recent acquisitions of mid-band spectrum for enhanced service capacity. Additionally, it mentions the company's strategy for spectrum management, including potential future acquisitions and license swaps to optimize network performance.

children.title: Human Capital Resources
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's commitment to human capital resources, emphasizing the importance of employees as valuable assets. It details the company's strategies for attracting diverse talent, fostering employee development through educational programs, and creating an inclusive work environment. As of December 31, 2021, Verizon employed approximately 118,400 individuals, with a focus on diversity in its workforce, including gender and racial representation. The section also highlights initiatives such as on-the-job training and tuition reimbursement to support employee growth and career advancement.

children.title: Patents, Trademarks and Licenses
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's ownership and licensing of various intellectual property rights, including patents, copyrights, trademarks, and domain names, essential for its business operations. It highlights Verizon's proactive approach in filing and registering these rights to protect its intellectual property both domestically and internationally. The section also mentions the company's practice of granting licenses to other companies, allowing them to utilize Verizon's proprietary technology, while noting that the expiration of these rights is not expected to materially impact operations. Additionally, it addresses the potential risks associated with third-party claims of infringement on intellectual property rights, which could lead to financial liabilities or operational changes.

children.title: Regulatory and Competitive Trends
children.summary: The section discusses Verizon's adherence to labor laws related to unionization and collective bargaining, particularly its relationships with the Communications Workers of America and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. It outlines the regulatory environment overseen by the FCC, including spectrum licensing and operational mandates, while noting that some competitors operate under fewer regulatory constraints. Additionally, it details Verizon's compliance with federal, state, and local regulations across various services, including implications of privacy and data security laws, public safety, and cybersecurity. The section also highlights the challenges Verizon faces in navigating these complex regulatory frameworks, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic.

children.title: Regulatory and Competitive Landscape
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's compliance with labor laws regarding employee rights to unionize and collective bargaining, highlighting its relationships with the Communications Workers of America and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. It details the regulatory environment in which Verizon operates, particularly the role of the FCC in overseeing wireless services, including spectrum licensing and operational mandates. The section also discusses the competitive landscape, noting that some competitors face fewer regulatory constraints, and emphasizes the importance of maintaining compliance with federal, state, and local regulations affecting wireless operations.

children.title: Federal, State and Local Regulation
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's compliance with various federal, state, and local regulations across its services, including wireless, broadband, wireline voice, and video. It details the regulatory frameworks governing these services, including the FCC's oversight, state-level regulations, and implications of privacy and data security laws. The section also addresses Verizon's commitment to public safety and cybersecurity, intercarrier compensation, and the regulatory responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the complexities and challenges faced by the company in navigating these regulations.

children.title: Wireless Services
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's compliance with employee rights regarding union representation and collective bargaining, highlighting its collaboration with the Communications Workers of America and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, which represent about 24% of its workforce. It outlines the regulatory framework governing Verizon's wireless services, emphasizing the FCC's role in overseeing spectrum licenses necessary for mobile and fixed communications. The section details the processes for acquiring spectrum, the implications of license renewals, and the regulatory obligations imposed on wireless carriers, including construction and coverage requirements. Additionally, it notes the potential challenges from state and local regulations regarding wireless service terms and facility approvals.

children.title: Broadband
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's broadband services, highlighting that the FCC classifies broadband as an 'information service' with a light regulatory touch, though potential shifts to stricter regulations are noted. It mentions ongoing litigation in California and Vermont regarding state-level broadband regulations. Verizon emphasizes its commitment to an open internet, ensuring consumer access to various content. The section also touches on related topics such as wireline voice services, video service regulations, privacy and data security laws, public safety, cybersecurity, intercarrier compensation, and the regulatory impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.

children.title: Wireline Voice
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's wireline voice services, which include traditional telephone and VoIP services. It explains that legacy telephone services are classified as 'common carrier' services, subject to strict regulatory oversight, while the regulatory status of VoIP is still under consideration by the FCC. Additionally, it notes that state public utility commissions oversee Verizon's telephone operations, with varying levels of regulation depending on the state. The section highlights Verizon's role as an incumbent local exchange carrier in nine states and the District of Columbia, and mentions the regulatory requirements for VoIP providers, including compliance with 911 and law enforcement assistance rules.

children.title: Video
children.summary: Verizon provides a multichannel video service that is regulated similarly to traditional cable services, requiring local or state-wide cable franchises and compliance with FCC rules. This section outlines the regulatory framework governing Verizon's video offerings, including obligations to local governments. It highlights the importance of adhering to specific regulations that apply to cable operators, ensuring that Verizon's video services meet legal standards. Readers can learn about the implications of these regulations on Verizon's operations and the competitive landscape of video services.

children.title: Privacy and Data Security
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's compliance with various privacy and data security laws at local, state, federal, and international levels, affecting all business areas including broadband and new technologies like AI and IoT. It highlights the implications of significant regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), which impose penalties for non-compliance. The section also discusses the increasing global focus on privacy legislation and its potential impact on Verizon's operations. Additionally, it touches on public safety and cybersecurity regulations, including FCC mandates for emergency communications and the regulation of cybersecurity practices in response to threats.

children.title: Public Safety and Cybersecurity
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's commitment to public safety and cybersecurity, highlighting the FCC's role in regulating emergency communications and the potential for increased cybersecurity regulations in response to cyber threats. It notes that Verizon does not use equipment from vendors considered national security risks and mentions regulations imposed by agencies for service continuity during natural disasters. Additionally, it touches on intercarrier compensation and network access regulations, as well as the impact of COVID-19 on telecommunications operations and consumer protection measures.

children.title: Intercarrier Compensation and Network Access
children.summary: This section discusses the FCC's regulation of intercarrier compensation, specifically the rates carriers pay each other for exchanging voice traffic and the terms for wireline business data services. It highlights Verizon's dual role as both a seller and buyer of these services, noting that the FCC is considering potential changes to the rates and conditions governing these exchanges. The section emphasizes the importance of interconnection payments in Verizon's operations and the regulatory landscape surrounding these services.

children.title: Regulatory Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic
children.summary: This section discusses the regulatory landscape affecting Verizon in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting various international, federal, state, and local policies aimed at health and safety. It notes the implementation of consumer protection measures that restrict how telecommunications companies operate and interact with customers. The section emphasizes the uncertainty surrounding the pandemic's impact on Verizon's business and the evolving nature of governmental responses, making future predictions challenging.

children.title: Information About Our Executive Officers
children.summary: This section directs readers to Part III, Item 10 of the Annual Report on Form 10-K for detailed information about Verizon's executive officers. It highlights the availability of various financial reports and corporate governance information on Verizon's website, encouraging stakeholders to review these resources. Additionally, it includes a cautionary statement regarding forward-looking statements, outlining potential risks and uncertainties that could impact future results, such as cyber attacks, natural disasters, and economic conditions.

children.title: Information on Our Internet Website
children.summary: This section provides information about the availability of Verizon's financial reports, including annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, and current reports on Form 8-K, which can be accessed for free on their investor website. It encourages stakeholders such as investors, media, and customers to review the posted information, which also includes corporate governance details and announcements regarding financial performance. Additionally, it includes a cautionary statement about forward-looking statements, outlining various risks and uncertainties that could impact future results, such as cyber attacks, natural disasters, and changes in the regulatory environment.

children.title: Cautionary Statement Concerning Forward-Looking Statements
children.summary: This section provides a cautionary statement regarding forward-looking statements made in the report, emphasizing that these statements are based on estimates and assumptions that carry inherent risks and uncertainties. It defines forward-looking statements and claims protection under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. The section lists various factors that could materially affect future results, including cyber attacks, natural disasters, public health crises, supply chain disruptions, competition, technological changes, and regulatory conditions. Readers are advised not to place undue reliance on these statements due to the potential for significant deviations from expected outcomes.

children.title: Item 1A. Risk Factors
children.summary: This section outlines the various risk factors that could adversely affect Verizon's business operations and financial performance. It covers operational risks such as cyber attacks, natural disasters, and public health crises, emphasizing the need for effective risk management. Economic and strategic risks are discussed, particularly in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic, supply chain dependencies, and competitive pressures. Regulatory and legal risks are highlighted, focusing on compliance with changing laws and regulations, including data protection. Finally, financial risks are detailed, including high debt levels, potential adverse credit conditions, and the financial burden of employee benefits.

children.title: Operational Risks
children.summary: This section discusses various operational risks that could adversely affect Verizon's business, including cyber attacks, natural disasters, and public health crises. It highlights the potential impacts of cyber attacks on networks and systems, which could lead to equipment failures, loss of sensitive information, and significant financial costs. The section also addresses the risks posed by natural disasters and climate change, which could disrupt operations and damage infrastructure. Additionally, it notes the adverse effects of public health crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, on customer behavior and operational capabilities, emphasizing the need for robust risk management strategies.

children.title: Economic and Strategic Risks
children.summary: This section discusses the economic and strategic risks faced by the company, particularly in light of the COVID-19 pandemic, which has led to decreased revenues and increased costs. It highlights the reliance on key suppliers and vendors for essential equipment and services, emphasizing the potential disruptions from geopolitical factors, supply chain issues, and litigation risks. The section also addresses the competitive landscape, noting the impact of new technologies and competitors on profitability, and the challenges posed by labor unions in renegotiating contracts that could lead to increased costs or work stoppages. Overall, it underscores the uncertainty in predicting the future impact of these risks on the company's financial condition and operations.

children.title: Regulatory and Legal Risks
children.summary: This section discusses the regulatory and legal risks that could impact the company's operations and profitability. It highlights the potential adverse effects of changes in the regulatory framework, including the need to maintain licenses and comply with federal, state, and international regulations. The section also addresses the implications of privacy and data protection laws, such as the GDPR and CCPA, which impose significant penalties for non-compliance. Additionally, it covers the regulation of broadband internet access services and the potential for changes in regulatory approaches that could affect business operations and revenue opportunities.

children.title: Financial Risks
children.summary: This section outlines the financial risks faced by Verizon, including significant debt levels totaling approximately $136.7 billion as of December 31, 2021, which could limit operational flexibility and increase vulnerability during downturns. It discusses the potential impact of adverse credit market conditions on borrowing costs and financing availability, as well as the implications of regulatory changes related to climate and net neutrality that could increase operational costs. Additionally, the section highlights the financial burden of pension and healthcare benefits for a large employee and retiree base, which may further affect profitability and funding commitments.

children.title: Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
children.summary: This section states that there are no unresolved staff comments regarding the company's financial reporting or disclosures. It indicates that the company has addressed all inquiries or issues raised by staff, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements. This lack of unresolved comments may reflect positively on the company's governance and transparency practices.

children.title: Item 2. Properties
children.summary: This section details Verizon's principal properties and their financial investments as of December 31 for the years 2021 and 2020. The total gross investment in property, plant, and equipment was approximately $290 billion in 2021, with a breakdown showing 76.9% in network equipment, 11.7% in land and buildings, and 11.4% in furniture and other assets. Network equipment includes various types of cable and related infrastructure, while land and buildings encompass facilities critical for operations, such as switching centers and administrative offices. The section highlights the importance of these assets to Verizon's operational capabilities and financial commitments.

children.title: Item 3. Legal Proceedings
children.summary: This section outlines that Verizon is not currently involved in any significant legal proceedings related to environmental regulations that could lead to monetary sanctions exceeding $1 million. It indicates the company's compliance with federal, state, and local environmental laws, suggesting a stable legal standing in this area. Readers can learn about the absence of major legal risks associated with environmental issues for Verizon.

children.title: Item 4. Mine Safety Disclosures
children.summary: This section, Item 4, Mine Safety Disclosures, states that there are no mine safety disclosures to report. It indicates that the company is not subject to any mine safety violations or incidents that would require disclosure under applicable regulations. This section is relevant for stakeholders interested in the company's compliance with mine safety regulations and its operational safety record.

children.title: PART II
children.summary: PART II covers Verizon's stock repurchase program, financial performance analysis, market risk management, and internal controls. It includes details on stockholder matters, management's discussion of financial results for 2021, and disclosures about market risks related to interest rates and foreign currencies. The section also presents financial statements, auditor reports, and confirms the effectiveness of disclosure controls as of December 31, 2021, while noting no changes or disagreements with accountants. Additionally, it addresses the implementation of a new ERP system and its impact on internal controls, with no material weaknesses identified.

children.title: Item 5. Market for Registrant’s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's stock repurchase program initiated in February 2020, which allows for the buyback of up to 100 million shares of common stock, although no shares were repurchased in 2020 or 2021. It emphasizes the company's strategy regarding equity management and shareholder value. Additionally, the section includes a Stock Performance Graph that compares Verizon's cumulative total returns over five years against the S&P 500 and the S&P 500 Telecommunications Services Index, showing Verizon's total return of $121.7 compared to $233.3 for the S&P 500 and $172.2 for the Telecom Services Index, indicating its relative market performance.

children.title: Stock Repurchases
children.summary: This section details Verizon's stock repurchase program authorized in February 2020, allowing for the buyback of up to 100 million shares of common stock. It outlines the conditions under which shares may be repurchased, including market conditions and capital allocation priorities. Notably, Verizon did not repurchase any shares during the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020, leaving the maximum number of shares available for purchase at 100 million as of December 31, 2021. The section provides insights into the company's approach to managing its equity and shareholder value.

children.title: Stock Performance Graph
children.summary: The Stock Performance Graph section presents a five-year comparison of cumulative total returns for Verizon, the S&P 500, and the S&P 500 Telecommunications Services Index. It illustrates how a hypothetical $100 investment made on December 31, 2016, would have performed by the end of 2021, with dividends reinvested. The graph shows Verizon's total return at $121.7, compared to $233.3 for the S&P 500 and $172.2 for the S&P 500 Telecom Services Index, highlighting Verizon's relative performance in the market over this period.

children.title: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive analysis of Verizon's financial performance and strategic initiatives for 2021, including key metrics such as operating revenues and net income. It details consolidated results, segment performance, and special items affecting financial outcomes, alongside insights into the operating environment and trends for 2022. The section also discusses liquidity, capital resources, and critical accounting estimates, highlighting Verizon's financial commitments and strategic transactions, including acquisitions and divestitures. Overall, it emphasizes the company's focus on network enhancements, customer experience, and market positioning.

children.title: Overview
children.summary: The Overview section provides a comprehensive analysis of Verizon's 2021 financial performance, highlighting key metrics such as operating revenues of $133.6 billion and net income of $22.6 billion, driven by strategic investments in 4G and 5G technologies. It details revenue contributions from the Consumer and Business segments, with notable growth in wireless services and the acquisition of TracFone. The section emphasizes significant capital expenditures of $20.3 billion aimed at network enhancements and the deployment of next-generation technologies. Additionally, it addresses the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on operations and outlines recent developments, including the deployment of C-Band spectrum and the sale of Verizon Media.

children.title: Highlights of Our 2021 Financial Results
children.summary: The section highlights Verizon's 2021 financial results, emphasizing its strategic focus on leveraging high-performing networks to drive growth in a digital marketplace. Key financial metrics include operating revenues of $133,613 million, operating income of $32,448 million, net income of $22,618 million, and cash flows from operations totaling $41,768 million, all showing growth from 2020. It underscores the importance of capital investments in wireless spectrum, network capacity, and advanced technology systems, particularly in 4G and 5G technologies, to maintain competitive advantage and enhance customer satisfaction. The deployment of next-generation technologies, such as the Intelligent Edge Network, is also discussed as a means to improve operational efficiency and expand business opportunities.

The section emphasizes the importance of capital investments in wireless spectrum, network capacity, and advanced technology systems to maintain competitive advantage. children.title: Cash Flows from Operations
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's strategic focus on leveraging its high-performing networks to drive growth and meet customer needs in a digital marketplace. It highlights the company's commitment to capital investments for acquiring wireless spectrum, enhancing network capacity, and developing advanced IT systems. Key financial results for 2021 are presented, including operating revenues of $133,613 million, operating income of $32,448 million, net income of $22,618 million, and cash flows from operations totaling $41,768 million. The section emphasizes the importance of network leadership and innovation in maintaining competitive advantage, particularly through the deployment of next-generation technologies like the Intelligent Edge Network.

children.title: Capital Expenditures
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's capital expenditures and strategic focus for 2021, emphasizing the importance of network capabilities in driving growth and customer satisfaction in a digital marketplace. It outlines the necessity of significant capital investments for acquiring wireless spectrum, enhancing network capacity, and developing advanced IT systems. The section highlights the deployment of new technologies, particularly in 4G and 5G networks, and introduces the Intelligent Edge Network aimed at operational efficiency. Financial results are summarized, showing an increase in capital expenditures from $18,192 million in 2020 to $20,286 million in 2021, alongside growth in operating revenues and net income.

children.title: Business Overview
children.summary: The Business Overview section provides a comprehensive analysis of Verizon's revenue streams, segmented into the Verizon Consumer Group and Verizon Business Group. It details the Consumer segment's $95.3 billion revenue in 2021, a 7.6% increase, and highlights its wireless and wireline services, including the acquisition of TracFone. The Business segment generated $31.0 billion, reflecting a 0.3% increase, offering communication services to businesses and government entities. Additionally, the section discusses Verizon's capital expenditures of $20.3 billion in 2021, focusing on network enhancements and the deployment of 5G infrastructure, while also addressing the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on operations.

children.title: Revenue by Segment
children.summary: This section details Verizon's revenue by its two reportable segments: Verizon Consumer Group and Verizon Business Group. The Consumer segment generated $95.3 billion in operating revenues for 2021, reflecting a 7.6% increase from 2020, and offers wireless and wireline services, including the recent acquisition of TracFone. The Business segment reported $31.0 billion in operating revenues, a modest increase of 0.3%, providing various communication services to businesses and government entities. The section also briefly mentions corporate and other revenues, which include unallocated expenses and results from divested businesses.

children.title: Verizon Consumer Group
children.summary: The Verizon Consumer Group section outlines the company's consumer-focused wireless and wireline communications services, highlighting its extensive wireless network and fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband offerings. It details the types of services available, including postpaid and prepaid wireless options, and the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, which enhances its prepaid service portfolio. The section also notes that the Consumer segment generated $95.3 billion in operating revenues for 2021, reflecting a 7.6% increase from the previous year. Additionally, it mentions the sale of residential fixed connectivity solutions and wireless network access to resellers.

children.title: Verizon Business Group
children.summary: The Verizon Business Group section outlines the company's Business segment, which offers a range of wireless and wireline communication services, including data, video, conferencing, corporate networking, and IoT solutions. It serves various customers, including businesses, government entities, and carriers, both domestically and internationally. For the year ending December 31, 2021, the Business segment generated $31.0 billion in operating revenues, reflecting a slight increase of 0.3% from the previous year. The section also briefly mentions the Corporate and Other category, which includes unallocated corporate expenses and results from divested businesses.

children.title: Corporate and Other
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's two main reportable segments: Verizon Consumer Group and Verizon Business Group. The Consumer segment focuses on providing wireless and wireline communication services, including fixed wireless access and a range of consumer devices, with 2021 revenues of $95.3 billion. The Business segment offers various communication services and products tailored for businesses and government clients, generating $31.0 billion in revenue for the same year. Additionally, the Corporate and Other category encompasses unallocated corporate expenses, investments in unconsolidated businesses, and historical results from divested entities like Verizon Media Group, impacting overall consolidated earnings.

children.title: Capital Expenditures and Investments
children.summary: This section details Verizon's capital expenditures and investments, highlighting a total of $20.3 billion spent in 2021, including $2.1 billion on C-Band related projects. It emphasizes the company's focus on enhancing its wireless networks and advancing technologies, particularly in 4G LTE and 5G infrastructure. The section outlines the strategy of network densification through small cell technology and the transition to fiber-based networks to meet growing demand for high-speed connections. Additionally, it notes the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on operations and mentions the successful deployment of C-Band spectrum reaching 100 million people by early 2022.

children.title: Global Network and Technology
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's strategic focus on enhancing its network capabilities through significant capital investments, totaling $20.3 billion in 2021, aimed at expanding 4G LTE and developing 5G networks. Key initiatives include network densification using small cell technology and the deployment of 5G Ultra Wideband in 87 U.S. cities. The transition to fiber-based networks is emphasized to meet the growing demand for high-speed data and video services, while the Intelligent Edge Network architecture aims to improve operational efficiency and support advanced services. Additionally, the section notes the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on operations and highlights the successful deployment of C-Band spectrum reaching 100 million people by early 2022.

children.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic
children.summary: This section discusses the significant impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on Verizon's operations during 2020, affecting the comparability of results with 2021. It highlights ongoing challenges due to new virus variants and emphasizes the company's commitment to employee and customer safety. While Verizon has not yet seen a material impact from these variants, the uncertainty regarding future effects on operations is acknowledged. The section also references a related discussion on business risks associated with COVID-19 in Item 1A Risk Factors.

children.title: Recent Development
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's recent developments, including the deployment of C-Band spectrum in January 2022, which reached approximately 100 million people in the U.S. by February 2022. It also mentions the sale of Verizon Media to an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, which closed on September 1, 2021, and highlights Verizon Media's operating revenues of $5.3 billion for 2021. Additionally, the section discusses ongoing investments in wireless networks and advanced technologies, totaling $20.3 billion in capital expenditures for 2021, aimed at enhancing network capacity and supporting the transition to 5G technology. The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on operations and the company's commitment to employee and customer safety are also noted.

children.title: Consolidated Results of Operations
children.summary: The 'Consolidated Results of Operations' section provides a detailed analysis of Verizon's financial performance for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It covers consolidated revenues, highlighting a $5.3 billion increase driven by growth in the Consumer segment, while noting a decline in Corporate revenues due to the sale of Verizon Media. The section also reviews consolidated operating expenses, indicating a decrease in overall costs, influenced by the sale of Verizon Media and operational efficiencies. Additionally, it discusses other consolidated results, including a turnaround in Other Income, changes in Interest Expense, and the Provision for Income Taxes. Finally, it explains non-GAAP measures like Consolidated EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, emphasizing their role in assessing Verizon's operating profitability and performance.

children.title: Consolidated Revenues
children.summary: This section details the consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020, highlighting a total increase of $5.3 billion (4.1%) in consolidated revenues, driven by growth in the Consumer and Business segments. The Consumer segment saw a revenue increase of $6.8 billion (7.6%), while the Business segment experienced a modest rise of $80 million (0.3%). However, revenues from Corporate and other segments decreased by $1.6 billion (17.3%), primarily due to the sale of Verizon Media, which resulted in four fewer months of operating revenues. The section also references further details on segment results in subsequent sections of the report.

children.title: Consolidated Operating Expenses
children.summary: The Consolidated Operating Expenses section provides a comprehensive overview of Verizon's operating costs, including the cost of services, wireless equipment, selling, general and administrative expenses, and depreciation and amortization. It highlights a decrease in overall costs in 2021, driven by reductions in traffic acquisition and personnel costs following the sale of Verizon Media, while also noting increases in rent and regulatory fees. The cost of wireless equipment rose significantly due to higher-priced 5G devices and increased sales volume. Additionally, SG&A expenses decreased by 9.2%, reflecting operational efficiencies and structural changes. The section also discusses the impact of asset sales on depreciation and amortization expenses, referencing further details in the consolidated financial statements.

children.title: Cost of Services
children.summary: This section details the cost of services for Verizon, outlining the components that contribute to these costs, such as salaries, materials, and network access. It notes a decrease in costs during 2021 compared to 2020, primarily due to reductions in traffic acquisition and personnel costs linked to the sale of Verizon Media. Additionally, it highlights increases in rent expenses for network capacity and regulatory fees. The section also discusses the cost of wireless equipment, which rose significantly due to higher-priced devices and increased sales volume, and provides insights into selling, general, and administrative expenses.

children.title: Cost of Wireless Equipment
children.summary: The cost of wireless equipment increased significantly in 2021, rising by $5.3 billion compared to 2020. This increase was primarily driven by a $3.6 billion shift towards higher-priced equipment, largely due to the growing demand for 5G-enabled devices. Additionally, there was a $1.3 billion increase attributed to a higher volume of wireless devices and accessories sold. This section provides insights into the factors influencing the cost of wireless equipment, highlighting trends in consumer preferences and market dynamics.

children.title: Selling, General and Administrative Expense
children.summary: This section details the Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) expenses for Verizon, which decreased by 9.2% from 2020 to 2021, totaling $28.7 billion. It includes costs such as salaries, benefits, advertising, sales commissions, and provisions for credit losses. The reduction in SG&A expenses is attributed to various factors, including operational efficiencies and changes in business structure following the sale of Verizon Media. Readers can learn about the specific components of SG&A and how they impact overall operating expenses.

children.title: Depreciation and Amortization Expense
children.summary: This section discusses the decrease in depreciation and amortization expense in 2021 compared to 2020, primarily attributed to the sale of Verizon Media. It highlights the financial implications of this sale on the company's overall expenses. Additionally, it references Note 3 in the consolidated financial statements for further details on the sale and its impact on financial metrics. Readers can learn about the relationship between asset sales and depreciation/amortization expenses.

children.title: Other Consolidated Results
children.summary: The 'Other Consolidated Results' section provides a comprehensive overview of Verizon's financial performance in terms of Other Income (Expense), Interest Expense, and Provision for Income Taxes for the years 2020 and 2021. It highlights a significant turnaround in Other Income, with a net gain in 2021 driven by pension remeasurement gains and changes in debt management. Interest Expense is analyzed, noting an increase in total interest costs despite a decrease in overall interest expense due to capitalized interest and lower rates. The Provision for Income Taxes is discussed, showing a rise in the tax provision linked to increased income before taxes, alongside a slight decrease in the effective tax rate. The section includes references to relevant calculations and notes for deeper insights into financial strategies and tax implications.

children.title: Other Income (Expense), Net
children.summary: This section details the Other Income (Expense), Net for Verizon, highlighting significant changes from 2020 to 2021. Key points include a net pension and postretirement benefits remeasurement gain of $2.4 billion in 2021, contrasting with a loss of $1.6 billion in 2020. Additionally, early debt extinguishment costs surged by $3.4 billion due to various redemption activities. The total Other Income (Expense), Net improved from a loss of $539 million in 2020 to a gain of $312 million in 2021, reflecting changes in interest income, pension costs, and other non-operating items. Readers can learn about the financial impacts of asset dispositions and debt management strategies during this period.

children.title: Interest Expense
children.summary: This section details the interest expense incurred by the company for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It reports total interest costs on debt balances, which increased by $524 million (10.9%) in 2021, while total interest expense decreased by $762 million (17.9%) due to higher capitalized interest costs and lower average interest rates. The average debt outstanding rose to $147,035 million with an effective interest rate of 3.6%. The section explains the calculations for average debt and effective interest rate, emphasizing their relevance for evaluating debt financing costs and leverage management trends. Additional notes reference spectrum licenses and debt transactions for further context.

children.title: Provision for Income Taxes
children.summary: This section details the provision for income taxes for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020, highlighting a 21.1% increase in the provision from $5,619 million to $6,802 million. The effective income tax rate slightly decreased from 23.4% to 23.1%, attributed to the sale of Verizon Media and a non-recurring tax benefit in 2020. The increase in the tax provision is primarily linked to a rise in income before taxes. Additionally, a reconciliation of the statutory federal income tax rate to the effective rate is referenced in Note 12 of the consolidated financial statements, providing further insights into tax calculations.

children.title: Consolidated Net Income, Consolidated EBITDA and Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA
children.summary: This section discusses Consolidated Net Income, Consolidated EBITDA, and Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures used to assess Verizon's operating profitability and performance. Consolidated EBITDA is derived by adding back interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization to net income, while Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA further excludes non-operational items and special items. These measures are intended to provide insights into operational effectiveness and facilitate comparisons with competitors by minimizing the effects of capital structure and accounting policies. The section emphasizes the importance of these non-GAAP measures in understanding Verizon's financial performance alongside GAAP measures.

children.title: Segment Results of Operations
children.summary: The Segment Results of Operations section provides a detailed analysis of Verizon's financial performance for the Consumer and Business Groups for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It highlights a 7.6% revenue increase in the Consumer Group, driven by wireless service and equipment growth, while operating expenses rose by 9.5%. The Business Group section notes revenue growth in the Small and Medium Business segment, contrasting with declines in Global Enterprise and Public Sector segments. Both subsections analyze operating income and EBITDA, emphasizing the impact of subscriber growth, cost structures, and technology shifts on revenue streams.

children.title: Verizon Consumer Group
children.summary: The Verizon Consumer Group section provides a comprehensive overview of the company's operating revenues, expenses, and financial performance for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It highlights a 7.6% increase in total revenues driven by growth in wireless service and equipment revenues, with specific figures detailing subscriber growth and the impact of the Tracfone acquisition. Operating expenses rose by 9.5%, influenced by increased costs in services and equipment, while SG&A expenses decreased slightly. The section also analyzes Segment Operating Income and EBITDA, noting variations in revenue across different customer segments. Overall, it offers insights into Verizon's financial dynamics, including revenue trends, cost structures, and operational efficiency.

children.title: Operating Revenues and Selected Operating Statistics
children.summary: This section details the operating revenues and statistics for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020, highlighting a total revenue increase of 7.6% driven by service and wireless equipment revenues. Key figures include a $2.5 billion rise in wireless service revenue, attributed to more subscribers and higher-priced plans, and a $2.6 billion increase in wireless equipment revenue due to a shift towards higher-priced devices. The section also provides data on wireless retail connections, churn rates, and average revenue per account (ARPA), indicating growth in wireless retail connections and a slight increase in ARPA. Additionally, it notes the impact of the Tracfone acquisition on revenue figures.

children.title: Service Revenue
children.summary: This section details the increase in service revenue for the year 2021 compared to 2020, highlighting a $2.5 billion rise in wireless service revenue driven by higher access revenues from postpaid plans, subscriber growth, and the acquisition of Tracfone. Additionally, Fios service revenue grew by $462 million, attributed to increased demand for higher broadband speeds despite a decline in voice revenues. The section provides specific figures on revenue changes, subscriber connections, and the impact of strategic acquisitions on overall service performance.

children.title: Wireless Equipment Revenue
children.summary: Wireless equipment revenue rose significantly in 2021, increasing by $4.3 billion (27.7%) compared to 2020. This growth was primarily attributed to a shift towards higher-priced equipment, particularly due to the rising demand for 5G-enabled devices. The section provides insights into the overall operating revenues, highlighting the impact of the acquisition of Tracfone and the performance of service revenues, which also contributed to the increase in total revenues. Readers can learn about the specific financial figures and trends in wireless equipment sales and their implications for the company's revenue growth.

children.title: Other Revenue
children.summary: This section discusses the components and changes in Other Revenue for Verizon, which includes non-service revenues such as regulatory fees, device protection offerings, and leasing income. In 2021, Other Revenue decreased by $462 million due to a price update in the device protection offering, while cost recovery surcharges increased revenue by $128 million. The section highlights the impact of product mix changes on revenue recognition and provides insights into the overall financial performance related to non-service activities.

children.title: Operating Expenses
children.summary: This section details Verizon's operating expenses for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020, highlighting a total increase of $5.7 billion (9.5%). Key components include a 6.2% rise in cost of services due to increased rent and digital content costs, a significant 30.4% increase in the cost of wireless equipment driven by higher sales volume and a shift to pricier devices, and a decrease in selling, general, and administrative expenses by 2.2%. The section also notes changes in depreciation and amortization expenses, reflecting asset usage and mix. Readers can learn about the financial impacts of operational decisions and market trends on Verizon's expenses.

children.title: Cost of Services
children.summary: This section details the cost of services and operating expenses for Verizon in 2021 compared to 2020. It highlights a $1.6 billion increase in revenue from wireless devices and accessories, alongside a decrease in other revenue by $462 million due to changes in device protection offerings. The cost of services rose by 6.2% to $16.6 billion, driven by increased rent expenses for network capacity, digital content costs, and device protection offerings. Additionally, the cost of wireless equipment surged by 30.4% due to higher sales volumes and a shift to pricier devices. Overall operating expenses increased by 9.5% to $65.3 billion, influenced by various factors including changes in selling, general, and administrative expenses.

children.title: Cost of Wireless Equipment
children.summary: This section details the cost of wireless equipment for Verizon, highlighting a significant increase of $4.8 billion (30.4%) in 2021 compared to 2020. The rise is attributed to a higher volume of wireless devices and accessories sold, along with a shift towards more expensive equipment, particularly 5G-enabled devices. Additionally, it discusses the overall operating expenses, which rose to $65.3 billion, influenced by various factors including increased costs in services and equipment. Readers can learn about the financial dynamics affecting wireless equipment costs and the broader implications for Verizon's operational expenditures.

children.title: Selling, General and Administrative Expense
children.summary: This section details the Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) expenses for Verizon, which decreased by $374 million (2.2%) in 2021 compared to 2020. Key factors contributing to this decrease include a $564 million reduction in provisions for credit losses due to improved payment trends and a $237 million decline in personnel expenses. Additionally, advertising expenses rose by $390 million as the company increased brand messaging efforts, while building and facilities costs increased by $121 million due to higher utility rates. Overall, the section provides insights into the components and trends affecting SG&A expenses during the fiscal year.

children.title: Depreciation and Amortization Expense
children.summary: This section discusses the increase in depreciation and amortization expense for Verizon, which rose by $284 million (2.5%) in 2021 compared to 2020. The increase is attributed to changes in the mix of depreciable assets and the usage of these assets by consumers. Readers can learn about the factors influencing depreciation and amortization in the context of Verizon's financial performance and asset management.

children.title: Segment Operating Income and EBITDA
children.summary: This section provides a detailed analysis of Verizon's Segment Operating Income and EBITDA for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It highlights a 3.8% increase in Segment Operating Income, totaling $29,955 million, and a 3.4% increase in Segment EBITDA, reaching $41,634 million. The section also breaks down operating revenues by customer groups, noting a revenue increase in the Small and Medium Business segment, while Global Enterprise, Public Sector and Other, and Wholesale segments experienced declines. Additionally, it includes key operating statistics such as wireless retail postpaid connections and churn rates, offering insights into customer growth and retention.

children.title: Verizon Business Group
children.summary: The Verizon Business Group section provides a comprehensive overview of the company's operating revenues, expenses, and performance across various customer segments for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It highlights revenue growth in the Small and Medium Business segment, while other segments like Global Enterprise and Public Sector experienced declines. The section also details operating expenses, including increases in wireless equipment costs and changes in selling, general, and administrative expenses. Additionally, it discusses the impact of technology shifts on revenue streams, particularly in Wholesale and Public Sector markets, and outlines the overall financial performance metrics such as segment operating income and EBITDA.

children.title: Operating Revenues and Selected Operating Statistics
children.summary: This section provides an overview of Verizon's operating revenues and selected operating statistics for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It details segment operating income, EBITDA, and revenue changes across various customer groups, including Small and Medium Business, Global Enterprise, Public Sector and Other, and Wholesale. The total operating revenues increased slightly by 0.3%, driven primarily by a 5.8% increase in Small and Medium Business revenue, while other segments experienced declines. Additionally, it includes statistics on wireless retail postpaid connections, Fios internet and video connections, and churn rates, highlighting trends in customer growth and retention.

children.title: Small and Medium Business
children.summary: This section details the financial performance of Verizon's Small and Medium Business segment, highlighting a revenue increase from $11,132 million in 2020 to $11,774 million in 2021, representing a 5.8% growth. It also provides insights into segment operating income and EBITDA, with operating income rising by 3.8% and EBITDA by 3.4%. The section outlines the services offered, including wireless and wireline communications, conferencing, and managed IT services, specifically targeting U.S.-based small and medium businesses. Additionally, it notes the overall increase in the Business segment's total operating revenues, driven primarily by this customer group, despite declines in other segments.

children.title: Global Enterprise
children.summary: The Global Enterprise section discusses Verizon's services tailored for large businesses and non-U.S. public sector customers. In 2021, revenues decreased primarily due to a $467 million drop in traditional data and voice communication services, influenced by market pressures. However, there were increases in wireless equipment revenue ($106 million), customer premise equipment ($90 million), and professional services revenue ($58 million). This section highlights the challenges and shifts in demand within the enterprise market, particularly in response to evolving technology needs.

children.title: Public Sector and Other
children.summary: The 'Public Sector and Other' section details Verizon's offerings to U.S. federal, state, and local governments, as well as educational institutions, focusing on wireless products, wireline connectivity, and managed solutions. In 2021, revenues in this segment decreased by $248 million due to customer migration to new solutions and a drop in wireless device sales, although there was a $217 million increase in wireless service revenue driven by higher connection volumes. Additionally, professional services revenue rose by $52 million, reflecting the shifting technology needs in remote business environments, particularly in education. The section highlights the specific challenges and trends affecting revenue in the public sector market.

children.title: Wholesale
children.summary: The Wholesale section details Verizon's wireline communications services, including data, voice, local dial tone, and broadband services provided to various carriers. In 2021, Wholesale revenues decreased by $338 million compared to 2020, primarily due to declines in traditional voice communication and network connectivity driven by technology substitution. This section highlights the impact of changing technology on revenue streams and the shift away from traditional services.

children.title: Operating Expenses
children.summary: This section details Verizon's operating expenses for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020, highlighting a total increase of $416 million (1.5%). Key components include a slight decrease in the cost of services, attributed to a decline in voice services, and an increase in costs related to wireless equipment and professional services. The cost of wireless equipment rose by $480 million (11.8%), while selling, general, and administrative expenses decreased slightly. Additionally, the section outlines specific factors influencing these changes, such as rising utility rates and regulatory fees.

children.title: Cost of Services
children.summary: This section details the revenue changes for Verizon's various business segments in 2021 compared to 2020. Small and Medium Business revenues rose due to increased wireless equipment and service revenues, while Global Enterprise and Public Sector revenues saw declines primarily from traditional service losses. The section also outlines the cost of services, which remained relatively flat, influenced by decreases in access costs and increases in direct costs and regulatory fees. Overall, it provides insights into the financial performance and operational costs associated with Verizon's service offerings.

children.title: Cost of Wireless Equipment
children.summary: This section details the cost dynamics of wireless equipment in 2021, highlighting a net increase of $987 million due to a shift towards higher-priced devices, offset by a $578 million decrease from lower sales volume. It also discusses the decrease in selling, general, and administrative expenses, primarily from reduced personnel costs and increased IT-related expenses. Additionally, it presents segment operating income and EBITDA figures, showing declines in both metrics compared to 2020, along with a breakdown of special items affecting income before taxes, including severance charges and losses on spectrum licenses.

children.title: Selling, General and Administrative Expense
children.summary: This section discusses the Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) expenses for the year 2021 compared to 2020. It highlights a decrease in SG&A expenses by $140 million, primarily due to reduced personnel costs and lower consulting fees, despite an increase of $71 million in IT and technology contract expenses. Additionally, it provides insights into segment operating income and EBITDA, showing a decline in both metrics, and details special items affecting income before taxes, including severance charges and losses on spectrum licenses. Readers can learn about the financial impacts of operational changes and special items on overall expenses and income.

children.title: Segment Operating Income and EBITDA
children.summary: This section details the Segment Operating Income and EBITDA for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. It highlights a decrease in segment operating income by $336 million (8.9%) and a decline in segment EBITDA by $338 million (4.3%). The changes are attributed to variations in operating revenues and expenses, including increased costs of wireless equipment and decreased selling, general, and administrative expenses. Special items affecting income before taxes are also outlined, including severance charges and losses on spectrum licenses, totaling $757 million in 2021 compared to $3,247 million in 2020. Additionally, it provides insights into the margins for operating income and EBITDA, which were 11.1% and 24.2%, respectively, in 2021.

children.title: Special Items
children.summary: The Special Items section outlines significant financial impacts related to severance, pension, benefits charges, spectrum licenses, early debt redemption costs, and asset dispositions for Verizon in 2021 and 2020. It details net pre-tax pension and benefits credits of $2.4 billion in 2021, contrasting with $1.6 billion in charges in 2020, and notes severance charges for both years. The section also reports a pre-tax loss of $223 million on spectrum licenses in 2021 and a $1.2 billion loss in 2020, alongside early debt redemption costs of $3.5 billion in 2021 compared to $102 million in 2020. Additionally, it highlights a pre-tax net gain of $837 million from asset sales in 2021, while noting a loss in 2020, providing insights into Verizon's financial strategies and market positioning.

children.title: Severance, Pension and Benefits Charges (Credits)
children.summary: This section details the financial impacts of severance, pension, and benefits charges and credits for the years ended December 31, 2021, and 2020. In 2021, the company recorded net pre-tax pension and benefits credits of $2.4 billion, primarily due to an increase in the discount rate assumption and differences in estimated versus actual asset returns. Conversely, in 2020, there were net pre-tax charges of $1.6 billion driven by a decrease in the discount rate. Additionally, severance charges of $209 million in 2021 and $221 million in 2020 are noted, reflecting voluntary separations. The section emphasizes the accounting policy of recognizing actuarial gains and losses in the period they occur and refers to additional details in Note 11 of the consolidated financial statements.

children.title: Loss on Spectrum Licenses
children.summary: This section details the financial impact of losses on spectrum licenses for Verizon, reporting a pre-tax loss of $223 million in 2021 from selling wireless licenses and a $1.2 billion loss in 2020 due to the conclusion of the FCC incentive auction for specific spectrum bands. It also mentions related financial activities, including early debt redemption costs and asset dispositions. The section emphasizes the competitive landscape of the telecommunications industry and Verizon's strategic focus on maintaining a strong customer base and financial health.

children.title: Net Early Debt Redemption Costs
children.summary: This section details the early debt redemption costs incurred by Verizon, reporting a pre-tax cost of $3.5 billion in 2021 due to tender offers and redemptions of securities, compared to $102 million in 2020. It highlights the financial impact of these transactions on the company's consolidated results. Additionally, it references Note 7 for further details on early debt redemptions, providing context for investors and stakeholders regarding Verizon's debt management strategies.

children.title: Net (Gain) Loss from Dispositions of Assets and Businesses
children.summary: This section details the net gain or loss from the disposition of assets and businesses for Verizon in 2021 and 2020. children.title: Forward Starting Interest Rate Swaps

children.title: Treasury Rate Locks
children.summary: This section discusses the use of treasury rate locks to manage interest rate risk, noting that gains and losses from interest rate fluctuations are recorded in Other comprehensive income (loss). The section also briefly mentions related financial instruments such as forward starting interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps, providing context for the company's overall risk management strategy.

children.title: Foreign Currency Translation
children.summary: The Foreign Currency Translation section covers the company's strategies for managing foreign currency risks through cross currency swaps and foreign exchange forwards. children.title: Cross Currency Swaps

children.title: Foreign Exchange Forwards

children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive overview of Verizon Communications Inc.'s business operations, accounting policies, and financial reporting practices. children.title: Description of Business
children.summary: Verizon Communications Inc. is a leading global provider of communications, technology, information, and entertainment services, operating through its subsidiaries. The company has two main segments: the Verizon Consumer Group, which offers wireless and wireline services, including fixed wireless access and fiber-optic products, primarily in the U.S.; and the Verizon Business Group, which provides a range of services including data, video, and IoT solutions to businesses and government entities.
